rows.label: Non-residents: IRPP on income from Chad
rows.value: Individuals, Chadian or foreign, with no domicile or residence in Chad are liable to IRPP on income earned in or from Chad
rows.note: Article 2 of the Code général des impôts; the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026. (article 4) restates paragraph I and leaves this rule unchanged.

rows.note: income from movable capital (articles 74 to 78 of the code). rows.note: gross dividends paid to individuals and companies based in the CEMAC zone. Article 77 V of the Code général des impôts as restated by article 9 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026.; 5% where the beneficiary is a CEMAC company holding at least 25% of the Chadian company.

rows.note: gross interest paid to beneficiaries based or domiciled in the CEMAC zone. Article 77 V as restated by article 9 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026.

rows.label: Withholding on dividends paid to beneficiaries outside the CEMAC zone
rows.note: gross dividends paid to beneficiaries based outside the CEMAC zone. Article 77 VI of the Code général des impôts, added by article 9 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026.

source.title: Loi portant loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (Tchad)

rows.label: Withholding on interest paid to beneficiaries outside the CEMAC zone and to non-residents
rows.note: gross interest paid to beneficiaries based outside the CEMAC zone; interest on receivables, deposits and guarantees paid to non-residents (final levy). Article 77 VI (added) and article 84 (amended) of the Code général des impôts, articles 9 and 11 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026.; interest on bank deposits under external loan and financing agreements is excluded from the article 84 levy. Subject to tax treaties.

rows.label: New companies in priority sectors: 50% corporate tax base reduction for ten years
rows.value: New companies in agriculture, agro-industry, market gardening, livestock, renewable energy, ICT and the creative and cultural industries get, for their first ten years, a 50% reduction of the registration duty and of the corporate tax base (corporate tax not below 15% of the normal tax) and exemption from the patente, the minimum tax, the flat tax and the apprenticeship tax
rows.note: Article 14 of the Loi de finances 2020, as amended in 2024, restated by article 6 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026. (which adds the creative and cultural industries and VAT exemptions for renewable energy and agricultural equipment).

source.title: Loi portant loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (Tchad)

rows.label: Special economic zones: 50% reduction of corporate tax for developers for ten years
rows.value: Developers in special economic zones (investment of at least FCFA 250 million) get for ten years a 50% reduction of corporate tax (at least 15% of the normal tax), the minimum tax, the patente and property taxes, and exemptions including the rental value tax, registration and stamp duties and the flat tax
rows.note: Article 2 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026.

source.title: Loi portant loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (Tchad)

rows.label: Vocational training tax credit (CIFP): 30% of training costs
rows.value: Companies taxed on a real or simplified basis may claim a vocational training tax credit of 30% of the cost of training their staff (35% where the training benefits women who are then promoted), set against corporate tax and carried forward two years
rows.note: Article 47 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026., replacing the apprenticeship tax exemptions of articles 180 to 186 of the code.

rows.label: Housing tax (taxe d'habitation): set by each commune
rows.value: A housing tax on occupied plots is due by the occupant (owner or tenant on 1 January); each commune sets its scope, base and rate; the proceeds are shared 50% provincial council, 50% communal council
rows.note: Article 772 of the Code général des impôts as amended by article 55 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026., which removes the national tariff; article 56 sets the sharing.

sections.title: Freelancers, contractors and the self-employed

rows.label: Impôt Général Libératoire (IGL): individuals with annual turnover below this amount
rows.note: Article 229 IV as restated by article 30 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026.; between FCFA 50 and 100 million, the simplified regime applies without VAT.

source.title: Loi portant loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (Tchad)

rows.label: VAT self-assessed by the buyer on supplies from small suppliers
rows.value: When a person outside the IGL, or an IGL taxpayer who has passed the FCFA 50 million threshold, supplies a service or sells goods to a VAT-registered business, the buyer self-assesses the VAT, pays it to the Treasury as VAT withheld at source and may deduct it
rows.note: Article 229 V, added by article 30 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026.

rows.note: payments by the Treasury on contracts and purchase orders for supplies, works and services. Article 121 of the Code général des impôts as amended by article 17 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026.; not applied to companies under the real or simplified regime holding an exemption certificate.

rows.note: Treasury payments to suppliers not on the DGI register of registered and known taxpayers (30% for repeat cases). Article 121 as amended by article 17 of the Loi de finances pour l'exercice 2026 (scanned copy on the customs website, read as page images), from 1 January 2026.

rows.value: From 1 January 2026, buses, coaches, taxis and minibuses (HS 87 02 10, 87 02 90, 87 03 21, 87 03 22) imported for urban and inter-urban transport are exempt from duties and taxes for five years; electric vehicles imported new get a 75% reduction of the taxable value, and electric vehicle chargers and charging stations are exempt

rows.label: New companies in priority sectors: 50% corporate tax base reduction for ten years
rows.value: New companies in agriculture, agro-industry, market gardening, livestock, renewable energy, ICT and the creative and cultural industries get, for their first ten years, a 50% reduction of the registration duty and of the corporate tax base (corporate tax not below 15% of the normal tax) and exemption from the patente, the minimum tax, the flat tax and the apprenticeship tax

rows.label: Special economic zones: 50% reduction of corporate tax for developers for ten years
rows.value: Developers in special economic zones (investment of at least FCFA 250 million) get for ten years a 50% reduction of corporate tax (at least 15% of the normal tax), the minimum tax, the patente and property taxes, and exemptions including the rental value tax, registration and stamp duties and the flat tax

rows.value: Companies taxed on a real or simplified basis may claim a vocational training tax credit of 30% of the cost of training their staff (35% where the training benefits women who are then promoted), set against corporate tax and carried forward two years
